entries.provenance: Placement of 2_Eksen_Sabit_SYM (the axis-2 column) inside Robot1_EKSEN1.stp -- 180 deg about Z plus t=(-10738.384, -0.108, 0).
entries.evidence: EKSEN2's root 2_Eksen_SYM has an IDENTITY placement and all its children sit at x~1500, y~-2980 -- the column's own master frame. The column's base plate (2_Eksen_Taban_Plaka_SYM) bottom face lands on the carriage plate (1_Eksen_Robot_Plakasi_SYM) top face to 0.40 mm under this matrix, with the 450x450 base fully inside the 950x714 plate.

entries.provenance: Same matrix as EKSEN2: EKSEN3 is exported in the same master frame, so it needs no transform relative to EKSEN2.
entries.evidence: BRep surface distance from EKSEN2's 2_Eksen_Robot_Plakasi_SYM to EKSEN3's Ic_Konstruksiyon_SYM_rev2 is 0.000 mm in NATIVE coordinates, with identical closest points (1507.0, -3216.8, -502.7). Two separately exported files cannot touch exactly unless they share a frame.

entries.provenance: Rz(+90 deg) plus t=(3376.008, -3570.168, -1252.860), placing Robot 2's rail as the MIRROR of Robot 1's about the bus's vertical longitudinal centre plane at cell Y = -137.2612 mm (the industrial partner's end-view slide: two parallel rails, bus centred, arms inward).
entries.evidence: Anchored on the carriage, which is provably the same hardware in both exports: Robot 1's 1_Eksen_Hareketli_SYM is 750.5 mm wide across the rail, Robot 2's 1_eksen_hareketli is 750.4 mm. Robot 2's rail runs along its native Y, so Rz(+90) turns it onto the cell X the bus runs along; native +Y (the carriage's home end) maps to cell -X, putting both carriages at the same cable-loop end. INDEPENDENT CHECK: the Z term was fixed by the carriage alone and lands Robot 2's carriage centre at cell Z -720.96 against Robot 1's -720.96, a 0.1 mm agreement that was not fitted.

entries.provenance: NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE EXPORTS -- DECLARED ASSUMPTION.
entries.evidence: Robot1_EKSEN5.stp contains no camera instance (0 hits scanning for Kamera/Blaze/Basler/D455/DT35), and Robot2_Kamera.stp is modelled centred on its own origin, so no upstream placed instance exists to read a matrix from. The head is positioned at render time by CAMERA_MOUNT in the gantry renderer, which hangs it below the axis-5 reducer. That is an assumption, not a measurement, and needs a figure from the industrial partner.
